svg.title: Concurrent logging: ownership, contention, and cost before and after the proposed redesign
svg.desc: Before uses two asynchronous runtime output workers, a shared allocator mutex, a structured sink mutex, and per-section atomic leases. Allocator links and encoder commit length share one section header. The proposal combines runtime output, separates metadata owners into physical blocks, bounds Grow allocation, and retains exclusive reclamation for overwrite. Counts reference review commit a18706a; proposed targets and illustrative numerical models are not measured speedups.

g.text: Who owns the bytes · where callers wait · what the redesign buys
AFTER proposed design · counts / models, no measured speedup
M = mutex L = listener mutex CAS = atomic ownership claim
AFTER · one owner per writable block
L: callbacks also run under locks
Mₐ · one shared allocator per physical log
Owns geometry, retained head / tail, section allocation, successor links
Rollover holds Mₐ through close + scan + flush + first encode
Shared RAM: 64 leases · generation / state / next · fault flag
SHARED HEADER · previous tail may belong to another stream
Encoder: IDLE → BUSY → IDLE; allocator sets LINK_PENDING on tail
Encoder may repair next link on release; allocator may seal idle sections
Overlap is coordinated, but ownership crosses the header boundary
Race symptom in review: normal contention can stop the output worker
Sync mode: same engine runs inline
Mₐ · one shared allocator per physical log
Owns descriptors, extents, links, retained head / tail, free-space geometry
Short allocation / publication critical section; first encode outside Mₐ
Grow: known geometry; overwrite: inspect only required oldest sections
SEPARATE PHYSICAL BLOCKS · same logical format for mmap + SD
Overwrite: writer vs reclaimer compete on state + generation
Idle section: revocable; writing section: never reclaimed
Stale handle → typed rebind before touching storage
Grow / StopWhenFull: per-entry reclamation CAS removal is a target
02 When a cycle gets better — or worse
Async moves output cost off the producer; synchronous output pays it inline. Structured logs stay on their callers.
One worker can delay CL behind KF
* Conventional async path with both outputs enabled; the distributed path already uses one combined worker.
Counts exclude fault checks / queue atomics. Structured rollover lock nesting: Mₛ → Mₐ → SD device lock.
failed append + close + retry; scan N
1 Mₐ for allocation; encode after unlock
rights / retry counts depend on final protocol
Scan N first, then claim / retire k
¹ Common rollover: 2 CAS failed append + 2 close + 2 successful retry; allocator claims / pending-link repairs add work.
Illustrative arithmetic · equivalent completed records and durability · no benchmark timings assumed
N existing sections: N extent visits / allocation
Per-section lookup may scan 64 lease slots
First CL encode C = 100 µs under Mₐ:
target: remove that 100 µs from lock hold
CL cost C; KF cost K every F cycles
Ideal isolated workers; I/O can dominate
Q = 64 pending bundles fills in ≈96 ms³
2 ms KF can delay the next CL by ≈2 ms
Combined rejection must account for both
² Empty log, one retained section per allocation, no wrap. ³ Fluid estimate Q/(λ−μ); ignores burst shape and slot limits.
Both: native encoder → stream section → mmap or SD; no staging buffer.
Both: stream sections interleave in allocation order inside one physical log.
Same payload pass; 0 new payload copies required by the proposal.
After: CL + KF encoding shares one worker; less cross-core coordination.
Cache hits, physical disk order and NUMA gains: not established.
Mₛ still serializes structured callers; Mₐ still serializes allocations.
SD: shared device lock per block read / write; payload I/O still serializes.
Mmap: routine rollover flushes whole backing maps today; bounded flush target.
512-byte blocks: two dedicated metadata blocks vs one adds 512 B/section⁴.
At 1 MiB payload: +0.049%; at 4 KiB: +12.5% metadata / payload.
⁴ Simplest illustrative layout; final block layout, recovery mechanism, RAM bookkeeping and flush guarantees remain to be specified.
Source map · BEFORE = a18706a, not a claim that every reviewed race remains in HEAD
